claude_proposed_widenings.name: force_drop_item
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Con save fail can cause the creature to drop the held object. No atom in v4 or the current surface models forcibly releasing a held item. This is distinct from force_move (repositions the creature) and apply_condition (no condition covers item release).
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or drop the object if it can

claude_proposed_widenings.name: object_contact_propagation — targeting for object-attached effects
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The damage applies to creatures 'in physical contact' with the attached object, not to the object itself. The current surface has no mechanism for an ongoing operation on an object attachment to propagate its effect to creatures touching that object. The object attachment kind targets the object as the anchor; there is no sub-targeting concept for 'creatures currently interacting with this object'.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Any creature in physical contact with the object takes 2d8 Fire damage when you cast the spell. Until the spell ends, you can take a Bonus Action on each of your later turns to deal this damage again

claude_proposed_widenings.name: conditional_or_save_outcome — branching within onFail
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The save_gate onFail is a conditional OR: 'drop the object if it can; if it doesn't drop, it has Disadvantage.' The current SaveSuccessOutcome / EffectAtom union accepts a single effect on fail with no internal branching based on the creature's ability or choice. This 'try A, and if A fails apply B' shape is not representable.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or drop the object if it can. If it doesn't drop the object, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks

claude_proposed_widenings.name: RiderExpiry.caster_turn_start
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Disadvantage rider expires 'until the start of your next turn' — the caster's turn start, not the target's. The existing RiderExpiry variants are target_uses_or_turn_start and end_of_next_turn, neither of which covers a caster-scoped turn-start boundary.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the start of your next turn
